primitives.name: Kinematic Acceleration Monitor
primitives.verbatim_quote: Blood oxygen, respiration, heart rates, velocity, acceleration/force, changes in direction, and position and many other factors are required in elite athlete training and coaching.
primitives.assumptions: Motion is captured in discrete time steps with constant sampling rate; acceleration integrates to velocity; forces act along primary axes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sensor drift exceeds 1% of baseline variance over 10-second intervals.

layer2.mapping: Maps raw accelerometer outputs to velocity and directional change using numerical integration and Kalman filtering techniques.
layer2.telemetry: Integrated velocity vector magnitude and direction change rate

primitives.name: Global Positioning System Tracker
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ability to measure and record athlete physiological information and positional information associated with athlete movement in real-time is critical in the process of athlete training and coaching.
primitives.assumptions: GPS signals are available and unobstructed; drift correction occurs every second.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When satellite signal loss exceeds 3 seconds or drift exceeds 5 meters per minute.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to inertial navigation systems where GPS provides absolute reference frames for correcting IMU drift.
layer2.telemetry: Position accuracy and drift rate over time windows

primitives.name: Physiological Data Aggregator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Blood oxygen, respiration, heart rates, velocity, acceleration/force, changes in direction, and position and many other factors are required in elite athlete training and coaching.
primitives.assumptions: Physiological signals are sampled synchronously with kinematic data; all metrics are normalized to standard deviation units.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When signal-to-noise ratio drops below 3 dB for any parameter over 5-minute window.

layer2.mapping: Aggregates biometric inputs into composite fatigue and readiness indices via principal component analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized physiological index values and inter-correlation matrices
